description.value: A 30-acre waterfront RV park and marina on Johnstone Strait, 6 km off Highway 19 between Port McNeill and Telegraph Cove, with rustic oceanfront tent sites alongside full-service RV hookups, a food truck, and a boat launch. Primarily an RV resort, but cyclists wanting a genuine wildlife-rich base on Northern Vancouver Island — orcas, humpbacks, and eagles regularly visible from camp — will find it welcoming.

address.value: 1 Alder Bay Road, Port McNeill, V0N 2R0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at alderbay.com is fully accessible and consistently names the business 'Alder Bay RV Park & Marina' (OSM says 'Alder Bay Resort' — flagged as a discrepancy). Phone (+1-250-956-4117) and postcode (V0N 2R0) are corroborated by the contact page, though the website lists only a PO Box mailing address rather than the OSM street address. Amenity evidence is drawn from the front-page amenity list and subpages: tenting sites, an on-site food truck (Roxy's Diner) and general store, free Wi-Fi, and an online booking system via Campspot are all explicitly confirmed; showers, laundry, hiker/biker-specific sites, and most cycle-specific amenities are not mentioned anywhere in the fetched content.
concerns: OSM name is 'Alder Bay Resort' but the website consistently uses 'Alder Bay RV Park & Marina' — OSM name may be outdated or informal.
OSM has no phone number; phone sourced entirely from website.
Website contact page lists only a PO Box mailing address (PO Box 1090, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0), not the street address in OSM — address contact_confirmed set to null.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active campground with tent sites, on-site food, and online reservations on a touring route along Northern Vancouver Island; useful stop for self-supported cyclists heading to or from Port Hardy.
enrichment_extras.notes: Free Wi-Fi is explicitly listed as a guest amenity on the front page, which may support device charging in a communal area, but no dedicated charging station for cyclists is mentioned.

wow_evidence: orcas, humpbacks, and eagles regularly visible from camp; tent sites and on-site food truck
